scraped.scraped_description: Whether you use ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, Copilot or Perplexity – generative AI poses massive problems: many results are inaccurate and politically problematic, the systems’ energy and water consumption is enormous. At the same time, they have become an integral part of everyday life. AlgorithmWatch has developed guidelines to help use generative AI responsibly.

name: AlgorithmWatch
tagline: A non-governmental, non-profit organization based in Berlin and Zurich that fights for a world where algorithms and Artificial Intelligence (AI) do not weaken justice, human rights, democracy, and sustainability but strengthen them.
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
known_funders: Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF)
Federal Ministry for Environment, Nature Conservation, Nuclear Safety and Consumer Protection (BMUV)
dependency_risks: grant-dependent (over 90% of revenue from grants in 2022)
EU regulatory environment changes could shift relevance
Big Tech resistance limiting research access (e.g., X/Twitter blocking)

policy_outcomes.description: Mandatory Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (FRIA) included in EU AI Act for high-risk AI deployments by public authorities — AlgorithmWatch cites this as direct result of three years of civil society advocacy it led or co-led.

Deployer transparency obligations in EU AI Act (public-sector deployers of high-risk AI required to register use and publish FRIA summaries) — AlgorithmWatch reports successfully persuading decision-makers on this requirement.
Matthias Spielkamp appointed to advisory council of German Digital Services Coordinator (DSC), elected by German Bundestag.
Expert testimony before committees of the Council of Europe, European Parliament, and German Bundestag on automation and AI.
Matthias Spielkamp served as member of the Global Partnership on AI (GPAI), the intergovernmental body coordinating international AI governance.

outcome_methodology: Self-reports policy wins citing specific legislative text changes campaigned for, supplemented by documented parliamentary testimony and expert appointments. No independent third-party verification of causal attribution.
documented_limitations: Acknowledges EU AI Act alone will not resolve fundamental power asymmetries in AI governance
Research access blocked by platforms (e.g., X/Twitter) limiting monitoring scope
EU database transparency carve-outs for law enforcement, migration, and national security remain unaddressed
Private-sector deployers of high-risk AI not required to register use in EU database
Work primarily EU/Western-European in geographic scope
jurisdictional_scope: European Union, primary focus Germany and Switzerland; Automating Society reports cover 17 European countries
failure_modes: Regulatory capture risk: advocacy through institutions may legitimise rather than constrain surveillance capitalism
Research access dependency on platform cooperation that can be revoked
Eurocentric focus may underrepresent Global South algorithmic harms
curation_criteria: Evidence-based, non-partisan; accepts funding only where it does not compromise ability to address issues freely; adheres to Transparency International Germany's Initiative Transparente Zivilgesellschaft
contributor_governance: gGmbH (charitable limited liability company) structure; three shareholders (Christina Elmer, Angela Müller, Matthias Spielkamp); supervisory board includes Sabine Leutheusser-Schnarrenberger
community_ownership: Shareholder-governed gGmbH; supporting membership open to the public but no community ownership of legal entity

elections_used_in.role: DataSkop research examined YouTube recommendation/search algorithms in run-up to election
Published platform risk-mitigation recommendations; research on AI chatbots producing election misinformation

government_partnerships.partner: Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF)

government_partnerships.nature: advisory council membership (Matthias Spielkamp, elected by Bundestag)
funding (FINDHR project on AI in recruitment)

ai_involvement: AI is the primary subject of research and advocacy rather than an operational tool. Uses AI monitoring tools in its own research (media-monitoring, llm-similarity repos on GitHub). Published guidelines (January 2026) on responsible use of generative AI by staff.
political_relevance_summary: Addresses challenges in algorithmic accountability by serving general public, policymakers, journalists.

movement_building_utility.notes: Provides information and analysis on AI/algorithmic risks relevant to public policy.

generalizability_notes: Open-source codebase facilitates replication and adaptation. Already deployed across multiple jurisdictions (11 countries), demonstrating cross-context adaptability.
